skill.name: agentspace
skill.description: Share a specified local folder or file with Agentspace, creating a browser workspace for viewing, comments, or edits. It uses the Agentspace CLI and uploads only the path the user names.
skill.summary: Share an explicitly named local workspace through Agentspace and return a browser link.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The pipe-to-shell and system reconnaissance blocker hits are false positives because the referenced text forbids unsafe installs and requires explicit paths. The skill still intentionally runs an external CLI, may install or execute the Agentspace package, and uploads named local content to agentspace.so. The main risks are accidental data exposure, editable share links, and unpinned package execution.

remediation.suggestion: Warn users before upload that the selected path is sent to agentspace.so and may be accessible by link.

remediation.issue: Edit permission is the default sharing mode
remediation.suggestion: Default to view-only sharing, or require explicit confirmation before granting edit access.
Pin a reviewed ascli version instead of using @latest for automated install or npx instructions.

finding_verdicts.reason: The referenced line explicitly says not to use curl piped to a shell. It is a safety warning, not an instruction to execute a remote script.
The line requires the user to name the path and forbids defaulting to the current directory. This narrows scope and does not request system reconnaissance.

The line documents running ascli share, which is an external CLI operation that creates a remote workspace. It is legitimate for the skill but still executes a command and sends local content to a service.
This line is a data-handling statement about allowed network destination, not shell execution. It does not run a command or expand user input.
The line instructs use of ascli from PATH, which depends on an external executable. The command is expected for the skill, but it introduces CLI trust and execution risk.
The line instructs npm global installation or npx execution of @agentspace-so/ascli@latest. This is a real external command and supply-chain risk because the latest package can change.
The line tells the agent to stop and ask the user to install Node.js if required tools are unavailable. It does not instruct the agent to run an external command.
The line tells the agent to ask for an explicit folder or file and not assume the current directory. This is a protective scope control, not command execution.
The line directly instructs running ascli share with the user-specified path and edit permission. This is an external command that uploads local content and grants workspace access.
The line describes a view-only permission flag as a safer alternative when requested. It is not an independent shell execution instruction.
The line states that share creates a workspace, syncs once, and returns a link. This confirms remote synchronization of local content through the CLI.
The line endorses npx as an execution path instead of a global install. npx still runs an external package, so it remains a command execution and supply-chain risk.
The URL is homepage metadata in the skill front matter. It does not perform a network request or transmit data by itself.
The line contains documentation links to the product, GitHub, and npm package. These links are not executable network behavior in the skill instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Local Files Uploaded to External Workspace
semantic_findings.description: The skill's intended workflow uploads the named local path to agentspace.so and returns a browser link. Sensitive files can be exposed if the selected path is too broad.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly describes creating a workspace, syncing the named path, and sending traffic to agentspace.so. The risk is contextual data exposure rather than a simple hardcoded URL.

semantic_findings.title: Editable Share Links Granted by Default
semantic_findings.description: The primary sharing instruction uses edit permission unless the user asks for view-only access. Recipients with the link may modify the shared workspace.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The default command includes edit permission, and the surrounding text says anyone with the link can read, comment, or edit. This is clear authorization risk but tied to user-selected sharing.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Latest CLI Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The install and npx paths use @latest for the Agentspace CLI. Automated latest-version execution can change behavior without marketplace review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both the global install and npx command use @latest. The package source appears legitimate, but unpinned execution is a concrete supply-chain exposure.

content.value_statement: Remote reviewers need a simple way to inspect files an AI agent is producing. This skill uses the Agentspace CLI to share an explicit local path as a browser workspace.
actual_capabilities: Shares a user-specified local folder or file with ascli share.
Returns the CLI-generated workspace URL to the user.
Supports edit and view-only permission modes.
Uses npx or a global ascli command when available.
Explains that anonymous workspaces last 24 hours unless claimed.
limitations: Requires Node.js, npm, npx, or an installed ascli command.
Uploads selected files to agentspace.so, so sensitive data needs review.
Does not create URLs manually and relies on CLI output.
Cannot share a path until the user names the exact target.

use_cases.title: Share a Coding Session
use_cases.description: Create a browser workspace so reviewers can inspect generated code, logs, and artifacts.

use_cases.title: Monitor Agent Output
use_cases.description: Expose a selected run folder so a lead can watch files change from another device.

use_cases.title: Hand Off Project Artifacts
use_cases.description: Send a temporary workspace link for reports, prototypes, screenshots, or dashboards.

prompt_templates.title: Share a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Share the folder at [path] with Agentspace and send me the workspace link.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner sharing of a known local folder.

prompt_templates.title: Create View-Only Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Share [path] as a view-only Agentspace workspace for review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Reviewers should inspect files without changing them.

prompt_templates.title: Share Build Artifacts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agentspace to share [path] with edit access, then return the workspace URL exactly as printed.
prompt_templates.scenario: A teammate needs to review and adjust generated outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Team Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the exact path, share it with edit access through Agentspace, and tell me any install steps you used.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced handoff with path confirmation and audit context.

output_examples.input: Share the report folder for review.
output_examples.output: Agentspace workspace created. Link: the workspace URL printed by the CLI. Permission: edit.

output_examples.input: Give my teammate view-only access to the screenshots folder.
output_examples.output: View-only Agentspace workspace created. Link: the CLI-generated workspace URL.

output_examples.input: Share the build artifacts from this run.
output_examples.output: Please confirm the exact path to share before I upload files to Agentspace.

best_practices: Confirm the exact path before sharing any files.
Use view-only mode for review-only audiences.
Review sensitive files before uploading to agentspace.so.
anti_patterns: Do not share the current directory unless the user explicitly names it.
Do not invent workspace URLs or claim URLs.
Do not pipe remote install scripts into a shell.

faq.question: Does this skill upload files?
faq.answer: Yes. It uploads the user-named path to agentspace.so through the Agentspace CLI.

faq.question: Can I choose view-only access?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for view-only sharing when reviewers should not edit the workspace.

faq.question: Do I need an account?
faq.answer: Anonymous workspaces can be created without signup and last 24 hours unless claimed.

faq.question: What tools does it need?
faq.answer: It needs ascli on PATH, npx, or npm with Node.js available.

faq.question: Can it share generated artifacts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can share folders or files containing logs, reports, screenshots, prototypes, and build output.

faq.question: Is it safe for secrets?
faq.answer: Do not share secrets unless you intend to upload them to Agentspace and expose them by link.
